variables.reason: The ledger's 'Ra' is explicitly the first-order (arithmetic) mean absolute roughness (symbols Ra; R_a) and the KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness defines Ra as the mean absolute deviation of surface height with si_dimension L (length). That record therefore establishes that Ra is a length quantity (L=1) and all other base exponents are zero, matching the candidate's before_si_exponents exactly and confirming the ledger usage (not the Rayleigh number).

The ledger's 'kt' is defined as the peak-to-valley height (kt; k_t), a roughness amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences; the KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height explicitly assigns si_dimension L (length) to this quantity. That supports L=1 and zeros elsewhere in the candidate vector, so the candidate exponents are correct.

The ledger's 'k_rms' is the root-mean-square roughness height (k_rms), and the KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines this canonical quantity as a length (si_dimension L). This directly supports the candidate's L=1, other exponents zero assignment.

The ledger's 'Sk' is surface-height skewness (third standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_skewness identifies Sk as a dimensionless standardized moment (si_dimension 1), which supports all zeros in the candidate exponent vector.

The ledger's 'Ku' is surface-height kurtosis (fourth standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_kurtosis declares Ku dimensionless (si_dimension 1), so the candidate all-zero exponent vector is supported.

The ledger's 'ES' is the effective surface (streamwise) slope: a mean absolute gradient of surface height. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope explains that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_dimension 1). That supports the candidate's all-zero exponent vector.

The ledger's 'Po' is surface porosity (void fraction). The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity as a dimensionless fraction (si_dimension 1) and notes it is used to describe surface/area porosity in roughness datasets; this directly supports the candidate vector of all zeros.

ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra is dimensionless because it is a ratio of two lengths (ks and Ra), so their units cancel out. The input parameters include lengths (Ra, kt, k_rms) and dimensionless statistical moments (Sk, Ku), slope (ES), and porosity (Po). Only the length quantities have dimensions, all others are dimensionless. Therefore, the output ks/Ra is dimensionless.
